citation: Ejigu, W., Selassie, Y.G., Elias, E., Damte, M. (2021). Integrated fertilizer application improves soil properties and maize (Zea mays L.) yield on Nitisols in Northwestern Ethiopia. Heliyon 7, e06074.
note: Single-season (2017/2018) on-farm RCBD, 3x3 factorial urea/NPSB (0/0, 50/50, 100/100 kg/ha) x compost (0, 5, 10 t/ha), 3 reps, Mosobo Kebele, Yilmana Densa, West Gojam, Ethiopia; maize BH-540. Not extracted (out of scope): post-harvest soil properties (Table 3), TGW, straw yield, harvest index, partial budget gross/net benefits and MRR (Table 5), fertiliser and grain prices. Source inconsistencies: Table 4 column header reads 'Compost (kg ha-1)' while methods and Table 5 use t ha-1 (rates 0, 5, 10 t/ha); text section 3.2 gives highest GY 6.06 t/ha while Table 4 prints 6.07 (table value used); Table 1 textural class 'Clay' while section 2.4 text says 'clay loam'; composting period given as 'from 2 Sep 2016 to 30 Feb 2017' (impossible date). Funded by CASCAPE (Wageningen University + Ethiopian universities). Scenario (b) comparator caveat: the 100/100 urea/NPSB arm is the trial's full mineral dose, not stated to be the extension recommendation (which the paper gives as 150 kg DAP + 100 kg urea) nor farmer practice (national average 45 kg DAP + 33 kg urea).
